application.name: ofetch
application.summary: A TypeScript HTTP client library that wraps the standard Fetch API with automatic JSON handling, URL/query composition, retries, timeouts, lifecycle hooks, and a normalized error type.
application.purpose: Provides a developer-facing HTTP client (`$fetch` / `ofetch`) used by other applications to make HTTP requests with sensible defaults (JSON body serialization, base URL + query composition, response parsing by content type, automatic retries on transient status codes, request timeouts) and a uniform error model (`FetchError`). It is infrastructure/library code rather than an end-user business application; the 'business' value is reduced boilerplate and consistent error/retry semantics for API consumers in the JavaScript/TypeScript ecosystem (published under the unjs/ungh ecosystem, per the example that calls the ungh.cc API).

domains.name: HTTP Client / API Access
domains.description: The core domain: issuing HTTP requests via the Fetch API and returning typed parsed data.

domains.name: URL and Query Parameter Composition
domains.description: Base URL joining, path normalization, and query string construction from structured objects.

domains.name: Request Payload Encoding
domains.description: Detection of payload-carrying HTTP methods, JSON serialization of request bodies, content-type/accept header defaults, and streaming/form bodies.

domains.name: Response Parsing and Content Negotiation
domains.description: Choosing a parser (json, text, blob, arrayBuffer, stream) based on the response Content-Type header or explicit responseType.

domains.name: Retry, Timeout and Cancellation
domains.description: Retry policy for transient HTTP status codes, retry delays, request timeouts via AbortSignal, and abort handling.

domains.name: Error Normalization
domains.description: Unified FetchError carrying request, options, response, data, and status information.

domains.name: Request Lifecycle Hooks
domains.description: onRequest / onRequestError / onResponse / onResponseError extension points for cross-cutting behavior.

terminology.meaning: The primary exported fetch function; `$fetch` is an alias of `ofetch`.
`$fetch.raw(...)` returns the full Response-like object (including `_data`) instead of only the parsed body.
The mutable per-request context object passed to hooks and to the error factory, holding request, resolved options, response, and error.
Normalized error thrown for network failures and 4xx/5xx responses; exposes request, options, response, data, status/statusCode, statusText/statusMessage.
Optional prefix prepended to relative request paths.
Object of query parameters; `params` is deprecated in favor of `query`. `undefined` values remove the parameter.
Explicit override of how the response body is parsed: json, text, blob, arrayBuffer, stream.
Custom function used to parse the raw response text (bypasses the default JSON parser).
When true, 4xx/5xx responses are returned instead of throwing a FetchError.
HTTP method carrying a request body: PATCH, POST, PUT, DELETE.
Set of HTTP status codes considered retryable (default 408, 409, 425, 429, 500, 502, 503, 504).
Delay in milliseconds between retries; may be a number or a callback receiving the context.
Request timeout in milliseconds, implemented via AbortSignal.timeout combined with any user-provided signal.
Experimental 'half' duplex flag, auto-set when the body is a ReadableStream or Node.js Readable.
Transport-level customization for undici (Node >= 18) or older node-fetch-native based runtimes.
Third-party safe JSON parser used by default to parse response bodies.

entityAnnotations.businessMeaning: Factory that builds an HTTP client instance (`$fetch`) with its own defaults, hooks, retry policy, and optional custom fetch implementation. It is the heart of the library's request lifecycle: resolves options, composes the URL, encodes the body, performs the request, parses the response, invokes hooks, and delegates failures to the error/retry path.

Central failure handler: decides whether a failure is retryable (not an active abort, retry enabled, status code in the retry set), applies the retry delay and re-issues the request, otherwise converts the failure into a normalized FetchError and throws it.

Builds the standardized FetchError for a failed request, composing a message of the form `[METHOD] "url": status statusText`, and exposing the original request, options, response, parsed data, and status fields as lazily-read properties.
Determines whether an HTTP method (PATCH, POST, PUT, DELETE) may carry a request body; used to decide body serialization and the default retry count (payload methods default to 0 retries).

Classifies a request body value as safely JSON-encodable, so that plain objects/arrays are stringified while FormData, URLSearchParams, Buffers/typed arrays, streams, and other exotic objects are passed through untouched.
Chooses the response parser from the server's Content-Type header: JSON media types to 'json', text/* and html/xml/svg to 'text', Server-Sent Events to 'stream', everything else to 'blob'.
Merges per-call options with the client defaults into a single resolved option set, combining headers (defaults then request-specific overrides) and merging query/params from both levels.
Combines default headers with request-level headers, letting request-level values win, and normalizes the result into a Headers instance.
Runs one or many registered lifecycle hooks sequentially against the current context, awaiting each so that asynchronous hook work completes before the request continues.
Concatenates a base URL and a path with exactly one separating slash, handling edge cases such as an empty or root base.
Applies the configured base URL to a relative request path, avoiding duplication when the path already starts with the base and normalizing trailing slashes.
Strips a trailing slash from a path so base/path joining is deterministic.
Serializes a structured query object into a URL query string: supports arrays (repeated keys), merges with an existing query string, deletes keys whose value is undefined, and encodes values.
Converts a single query parameter value to its string form: null becomes an empty value, numbers/booleans are stringified, and objects are JSON-encoded.
Demonstration of the library's headline feature: generic typing of the response payload, so a GitHub-repository-like record is returned strongly typed at compile time.
Test helper that aborts an in-flight request via an AbortController, verifying that an explicit abort is not silently retried and surfaces an aborted error.
Manual scratch script that calls a URL returning HTTP 500, used to observe error output and stack traces outside the automated test suite.

applicationFacts: The public API surface is the `$fetch` function (also exported as `ofetch`), with `raw`, `native`, and `create` variants for full-response access, direct platform fetch access, and deriving pre-configured clients.

Clients can be specialized through `createFetch`/`$fetch.create`, which merges defaults (baseURL, headers, query, timeout, retry) and supports an injected fetch implementation for testing or polyfills.

Request bodies on payload methods are auto-serialized to JSON and get `content-type: application/json` and `accept: application/json` headers unless the caller specifies otherwise; `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` bodies are encoded as URL-encoded form data.
FormData, URLSearchParams, Buffers, ReadableStream, and Node.js Readable bodies are passed through unserialized; streaming bodies automatically enable `duplex: 'half'`.
Responses are parsed according to the Content-Type header by default; JSON is parsed with the `destr` safe parser, and a custom `parseResponse` function can override parsing entirely.
Bodyless responses (101, 204, 205, 304) and HEAD requests yield no parsed data.

By default, responses with status 400-599 raise a FetchError unless `ignoreResponseError` is set; the error exposes request, options, response, parsed data, status/statusCode, and statusText/statusMessage.

Retry defaults: one attempt for non-payload methods, zero for payload methods; retryable status codes are 408, 409, 425, 429, 500, 502, 503, 504 and can be overridden via `retryStatusCodes`; delay supports a fixed number or a per-context callback.
Timeouts are implemented with AbortSignal.timeout and combined with any user-provided signal via AbortSignal.any; timeouts are not auto-retried while explicit aborts are reported as abort errors.
Four lifecycle hooks are supported - onRequest, onRequestError, onResponse, onResponseError - each accepting a single hook or an array, executed sequentially.
The example demonstrates consumption against the ungh.cc GitHub API, indicating the library's usage within the unjs/ungh open-source tooling ecosystem.
Tests spin up a local h3 HTTP server with routes for ok, echo, params, binary, 403, 408, 204, and slow timeout scenarios to validate client behavior end-to-end.
